claims.explanation: SB-366791 is annotated as a TRPV1 antagonist, but the selective killing pattern is not explained by TRPV1 expression because TRPV1 is a sensory-neuron channel rarely expressed in cancer lines. The pattern instead tracks with TP53 mutation and, more specifically, with co-occurring alterations in RAS/RTK-MAPK and PI3K pathway genes (KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, PTEN, NF1, EGFR, MAP2K1), suggesting that the drug's cytotoxicity is enhanced in cells with combined p53 loss and proliferative/survival pathway activation. The virtual-cell response showing up-regulation of JUN and down-regulation of NFKBIA and CHEK2 is consistent with stress/DNA-damage and MAPK-related signaling contributing to sensitivity.

KRAS mutation appears in multiple selectively killed lines (SNU410, KPNSI9S, OV7, GSU, CL11 is least affected) and is a known MAPK/PI3K activator
BRAF mutation appears in several killed lines (SNUC5, HEC265, LOXIMVI, UACC62) and is a MAPK pathway activator
PIK3CA mutation appears in multiple killed lines (HGC27, SNUC5, MKN1, KYSE510 is least affected) and activates PI3K survival signaling
PTEN mutation/loss appears in several killed lines (FTC133, ZR751, UACC62) and activates PI3K signaling
NF1 mutation appears in killed lines (FTC133, LOXIMVI) and activates RAS-MAPK signaling
EGFR mutation appears in killed line KYSE270 and is a receptor tyrosine kinase activating MAPK/PI3K
MAP2K1 mutation in NCIH1437 directly activates MAPK signaling
RB1 mutation appears in several killed lines (FTC133, OV7, GSU) and may reflect a proliferative, checkpoint-deficient state
TRPV1 is the annotated target but is not expressed in most cancer lines; high expression could sequester drug or mediate survival signaling, though direct evidence in these lines is absent
Virtual cell shows CHEK2 down-regulation, suggesting DNA-damage checkpoint impairment may enhance sensitivity
Virtual cell shows JUN up-regulation, consistent with stress/MAPK pathway activation contributing to drug response
